preamble: The voiced alveolar affricate [dz] palatalizes to the alveolo-palatal [dʑ] before the high front vowel [i], as the tongue body rises toward the vowel. In Seneca (Iroquoian), /dz/ before [i] varies freely with [dʑ] (Chafe 1967). In Japanese, the voiced coronal sibilant is [dz] (or [z]) before /u/, as in ズボン [dzɨbõɴ] 'trousers', but [dʑ] (or [ʑ]) before /i/, as in 時間 [dʑikaɴ] 'time'. Both cases are allophonic palatalizations, not phonemic mergers.

examples.note: Optional palatalization in free variation with [dz] before [i] (Chafe 1967: 6).
The phoneme, usually written /z/ and treated by some analysts as /dz/, varies between affricate and fricative; before /i/ it is alveolo-palatal, as in /mozi/ [modʑi ~ moʑi] 'letter'.

sources: Chafe, W. (2015). A Grammar of the Seneca Language. University of California Press. https://doi.org/10.1525/9780520961647
